narratives.Description: Build the fictional Node.js capstone runtime that creates one unique OS-temporary Git repository and carries a learner through a complete solo Directive-managed change. The helper must enforce the no-remote, exact-pin, narrow-write, ordered-evidence, reset, archive, and protected-root boundaries independently of the learner-facing walkthrough.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Add a minimal fictional work-items CLI, supplied tests, Directive project state, Taskfile gate, evidence verifier, and a guarded helper that creates and advances an isolated capstone attempt without writing in the training repository.
2. Add test-first positive and adversarial coverage for creation, lifecycle order, allowed product edits, immutable tests and gates, simulated review evidence, reset, archive, path traversal, symlinks, Git redirection, remotes, and platform-specific path handling; add a pinned GitHub Actions matrix for the same fixture suite.
narratives.UserStory: As a Directive learner, I want a guarded disposable repository for the complete solo lifecycle, so that I can practice implementation and closeout without risking training or business repositories.

narratives.PortabilityAmendment: On 2026-09-12 David approved changing the capstone native proof from Node.js 20.20.2 to Node.js 24.20.0 after CI established that exact Directive 0.112.0 imports node:fs globSync, which is unavailable before Node.js 22. Preserve Node.js 20 compatibility for the fictional application source, the exact Directive pin, all three native OS jobs, read-only permissions, and no-remote behavior. Compare Windows Git roots by filesystem identity so equivalent short and long path spellings do not weaken the existing root guards. Merge remains separately gated.

items.title: Prove fixture behavior and platform boundaries

narrative.Acceptance: When the focused Node suite runs, it passes positive and negative fixture cases on the authoring platform; the pinned macOS, Ubuntu, and Windows workflow runs only the disposable no-remote fixture tests with read-only repository permissions; and learner-facing platform claims remain candidate until corresponding native evidence is observed.

Given a failed or completed attempt, reset creates a fresh unique attempt without overwriting the prior repository or its evidence, and archive or cleanup accepts only one explicit canonical attempt root outside protected locations, refuses traversal, symlink and Git-redirection escapes, and preserves recoverable evidence according to the documented disposition.

items.title: Create an exact, isolated starting repository

narrative.Acceptance: Given an explicit create command from outside the training repository, the helper creates a unique OS-temporary Git repository on branch training/capstone with no remotes, the exact learner Directive pin, a fictional work-items CLI, supplied failing tests, deterministic project gates, and exactly one proposed capstone story; it refuses the training root, business-like roots, broad workspace roots, and reused destinations before writing.
